description.narrative: IFC proposes an equity investment of up to US$60 million and an additional co-investment envelope of up to US$40 million under the delegated authority framework, in Multiples Private Equity GIFT Fund IV (the Fund or Fund IV), a mid-market private equity (PE) fund focused on growth transactions in India and, together with Multiples Private Equity Fund IV (India Fund) is targeting US$800 million to US$1 billion in total commitments. Consistent with its prior funds, Fund IV will continue to focus on its key strengths of targeting growth stage mid-market companies in financial services, consumer, technology, healthcare and pharmaceuticals sectors. The Fund is expected to size its average ticket per company in the range of US$50-US$150 million in 10-12 companies.

The Fund will increase access to growth stage capital and support value creation for 10-12 mid-market companies in India. While India has significant PE investment volumes with a relatively small gap in access to capital compared to other emerging markets, mid-cap companies still struggle to attract as much interest from investors as venture capital (VC) or larger-ticket deals. Following the strategy Multiples developed over previous funds, the Fund will support its investees' growth through organizational and operational support. Beyond the project, IFC's continued support to Multiples will also strengthen the competitiveness of the mid-cap market segment via demonstration channels and encourage other fund managers to raise funds targeting this segment. The Fund's success will also attract other domestic institutional investors in follow-on funds, increasing the market's depth and continue to reduce the need for DFI involvement. Multiples is also one of the few female-led funds active in the Indian PE market. Women are significantly underrepresented among the investment decision-makers at fund managers, where globally only 12 percent of senior employees and only 20% of overall employees are women. The Indian PE industry has lagged even these low global averages, with female representation within PE at only 9 percent. While achieving gender parity in the Indian fund management industry is a longer-term objective, Multiples continued success will send a strong positive signal in female-led managers and further build momentum towards greater female representation in the Indian PE market
